newsitem.title: UK: Strong new crop pulls LIFFE wheat higher.
newsitem.headline: Strong new crop pulls LIFFE wheat higher.

text.p: LIFFE wheat rose on Tuesday, with worries over dry weather and general sentiment that supply next year could be tight pushing up new crop positions, and a knock on effect on the old crop.

November was the most active month on wheat, with 363 lots done. It last traded 1.75 stg higher at 99.50 stg. On the old crop May rose 1.65 stg to 97.90 stg on volume of 260 lots. Total wheat volume was 830 lots.
"The undertone for the new crop has been established as firm," one trader said, citing ideas on world-wide grains production, from the International Grains Council in particular.
"The world situation could be reasonably tight," he said, especially if there are weather problems in any region.
Firmness in the French market, inspired by the same sentiment, helped bring the old crop back up.
"Old crop wheat was cheaper than French new crop when we started this morning," the trader pointed out.
New crop had led, but as long as the firm tone continued in France and the rest of the continent, it was likely to pull old crop up with it.

There was also an element of correction in Tuesday's recovery. "Call me old fashioned, but 6.50 stg in a few days is a big move," he said, referring to recent losses. "This recovery is a bit of a correction."
May wheat went from an open of 102.55 stg on April 1 down to 96.25 stg on Monday.
The trader was pleased with the volume. "400 lots of new crop can't be bad," he said.
Barley was also firm. Only November traded, rising 2.00 stg to 96.25 stg, on volume of 28 lots.
Weather fears are becoming more an element in traders' thinking across Europe. There are fears in France that the new crop might be reduced if there is no rain in the next 10 days.
